task.title: The multi-process test's concurrent-create half passes even if every create is refused
task.description:
internal/cli/multiprocess_test.go:29-71 (TestBuiltBinariesMutateOneRepositoryConcurrently, added in PR #33 by commits 29c8daa and 76395e4).

The update half of this test demands forward progress: after the contended updates it asserts `if accepted == 0 { t.Fatalf(...) }` (multiprocess_test.go:96-98). The create half has no equivalent. If all six concurrent creates were refused with a tolerated projection-contention message, `ids` would be empty, the `taskRefCount(t, repository) != len(ids)` check would compare 0 to 0 and pass, all six would then be retried serially through `mustRunBinary` and succeed, and the final `len(listed) != writers` check would see 6 and pass. A regression that made concurrent creation fail 100% of the time under contention - the precise scenario this test exists to cover for a multi-agent beta - would leave the suite green.

Fix: after the loop over `created`, add `if len(refused) == writers { t.Fatalf(...) }` naming the outcomes, so at least one concurrent create must be accepted.

Deferred from PR #33 rather than fixed there because the PR was closing out the two major review findings (the README inline-publication claim and the cold module cache in buildWorkbookBinary) and this needs a moment of thought about the right floor. Requiring `accepted >= 1` is almost certainly safe - each tolerated refusal message ("task refs changed during projection rebuild", "activate projection cache after rebuild", "refresh projection cache after a concurrent update") describes another process having moved refs, which implies a winner - but the assertion runs on shared CI runners under real contention, so whoever takes this should confirm the floor cannot flake before tightening it.
